messages:
mike: hey team — quick sanity check. we have a customer hitting weird 403s when our node SDK tries to impersonate a service account across org boundaries. same SA works from gcloud CLI. any obvious pitfalls on the client side?

anya: did they mean cross-project or cross-organization? those behave a bit differently for token audiences.

mike: cross-organization (org A service account impersonates target in org B via our app running in org A). error: "permission denied: iam.serviceAccounts.getAccessToken" from the token exchange call.

devex-bot: FYI automated note: if impersonation is used, ensure the impersonating principal has roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator on the target SA. Docs: https://example.internal/iam/impersonation

kevin: common gotcha: CLI may be using your user creds that have org-level perms; SDK might be using workload identity or a different service account that lacks tokenCreator. can you paste the snippet of how the SDK is requesting the JWT?

mike: pasted below (node):
```js
const jwt = createJwt({iss: SA_EMAIL, aud: `https://tokens.example.com/${TARGET_SA}`, scope: 'https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform'});
const resp = await fetch(tokenExchangeUrl, {method: 'POST', headers:{Authorization:`Bearer ${jwt}`}});
```

olivia: hmmm, two notes: 1) audience for exchange endpoints usually expects the full resource name, not a URL prefix — double-check what the token service expects. 2) you might need to use the impersonation endpoint that accepts a target_principal param instead of sending raw JWT to a generic token URL.

luis: also check the JWT claims — if you're using OIDC style flow, the `aud`==client_id vs `aud`==token endpoint mismatch can lead to silent rejects. If gcloud is succeeding, run `gcloud auth print-identity-token --impersonate-service-account=${SA_EMAIL}` and compare claims.

mike: thanks — i'll diff the tokens. one more thing: when the node client hits this during streaming reauth, we sometimes see a race where the SDK uses a cached short-lived token for the wrong project. any suggestions for robust caching strategy?

anya: prefer a token cache keyed by (service_account_email, target_project, scope_set) and include issued_at. skew guard: refresh at 85% of lifetime. for streaming, make refresh opportunistic on first 5 token uses to avoid thundering herd on cold start.

kevin: in python we had to special-case streaming iterators — if token refresh fails, yield a soft error frame to the stream consumer and trigger background refresh, rather than block the main RT loop. less surprising to apps.

olivia: code review ping @kevin @anya — can we add a small utility in sdk-auth to canonicalize audience and a helper to build the impersonation payload? i can draft a patch. :+1:

kevin: ack, will review. if you include a sample curl and a unit test that mocks token endpoint behavior (403 vs 200) that should catch regressions.

mike: i'll run the gcloud diff, then try the audience change and the cache key tweak. will post results here. thanks all :rocket:

devex-bot: checklist added to thread: [run gcloud token diff, change aud to resource name, add cache key per SA+project+scopes, add streaming soft-error path]

mike: update — gcloud token shows aud: "https://tokens.example.com/target-principal:impersonate" while our SDK used `https://tokens.example.com/${TARGET_SA}`. swapping that fixed the 403. following up on cache and review PRs next. :tada:
